Why enterprise AI deployment keeps failing

false debts sent in Australia's Robodebt
Australia · 2016–2020
A$1.8Bclass-action settlement

Robodebt

An automated system averaged people's yearly income across every fortnight and sent debt notices to welfare recipients, leaving them to prove they owed nothing. Around A$1.75 billion was recovered unlawfully, and a Royal Commission followed.

Netherlands · 2019–2021
26,000+parents wrongly accused

The childcare benefits scandal

A self-learning risk algorithm flagged families for benefit fraud, hitting lower-income and dual-nationality families hardest. Parents were forced to repay tens of thousands of euros with no real way to appeal, more than a thousand children were removed from their homes, and the government resigned.

Michigan, USA · 2013–2015
93%error rate

MiDAS, the fraud detector

A fraud-detection system falsely accused around 40,000 residents. Wages were garnished, bank accounts drained and businesses destroyed. The state abandoned it and paid hundreds of millions in settlements.

Canada · 2022–2024
$812awarded to the passenger

The airline chatbot that invented a policy

An airline's chatbot explained a bereavement refund that didn't exist, and the passenger who relied on it was refused. The airline argued the chatbot was "a separate legal entity responsible for its own actions." The tribunal called that remarkable, and made the airline pay.

New York, USA · 2023
6court cases that never existed

The lawyer and the fake cases

A lawyer's ChatGPT research produced six court decisions, with quotes and docket numbers, that were made up. When he asked it to double-check, it assured him they were real. He was sanctioned $5,000.

Hong Kong · 2024
$25Mtransferred in one call

The video call where everyone was fake

A multinational's finance employee joined a video call with the company's CFO and four colleagues. Every one of them was a real-time deepfake, and he transferred $25 million.

AI forgets, hallucinates, and says the job is done when it isn't.

When AI hallucinates, it's the people who pay the price.

Sources: AI Incident Index · AI Companion Mortality Database · Stanford 2026 AI Index · The Architecture of Algorithmic Harm (Robodebt Royal Commission, Dutch parliamentary inquiry, Moffatt v. Air Canada, Mata v. Avianca).

The product

Hand it the paperwork.Get your day back.

BlueSpark™ automates your daily work on the computer you already have, without changing the systems you use.

Join the Founding 500Book a consultation

A day with BlueSpark™

From morning to night

  1. Morning.

    You drop a folder of invoices, contracts and emails into BlueSpark™. It reads every page and remembers what matters.

  2. Midday.

    It works through the pile on its own: matching invoices, flagging a clause that changed, preparing the summary you need. Every number it shows you comes from your own files.

  3. When something’s off.

    It doesn’t guess. It tells you exactly what it couldn’t confirm, so you decide.

  4. Night.

    While you sleep, BlueSpark™ reviews the day and learns how you like things done. Tomorrow, it’s a little better at your job.

How it’s built

An AI built like a brain.

Other AIs are a model with features. BlueSpark™ is an organism with a model inside.

01

It remembers.

BlueSpark™ has a neuromorphic brain, a memory that works the way yours does. Important things get stronger every time you use them. Clutter fades away. Close your laptop on Friday, open it on Monday, and it knows exactly where you left off.

02

It thinks about its own thinking.

BlueSpark™ is the first AI with metacognition. Before it acts, it asks itself: am I sure? If it isn’t, it tests its ideas, checks the facts, and tells you plainly.

03

It sleeps.

Every night, BlueSpark™ goes over the day’s work, keeps the lessons that proved true, and files away the mistakes so it never repeats them.

It grows with you.

The longer you use it, the better it gets at your job. Its intelligence comes from your work, not from someone else’s data.

Why you can trust it

The AI suggests. BlueSpark™ decides.

Every AI can sound confident. BlueSpark™ has to prove it.

Nothing counts until it’s checked.

When the AI says a job is done, BlueSpark™ doesn’t take its word for it. It checks the real result: the file exists, the number matches your document, the task actually happened.

It keeps a record.

Every step is written down before it happens. Nothing gets done twice by accident, and you can always see who did what, and why.

It knows when to stop.

If BlueSpark™ can’t confirm something, it doesn’t guess. It stops, tells you what it couldn’t check, and suggests what to do next.

It doesn’t hallucinate into your memory.

Anything unproven is kept out of what BlueSpark™ learns, so one bad guess never becomes a permanent “fact.”

Your files stay home.

Your documents, memory and history live on your own machine. No big IT project, no expensive consultants.
